lead: Round Rock plumbing deals with clay and limestone soils, hard water and fast-growing subdivisions. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Round Rock.
risk: slab leaks, hard water scale and burst pipes in hard freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, hard water and frozen pipes
why: Most Round Rock homes were built after 1980 on slabs over clay and limestone. Shifting clay stresses supply lines under the floor, and homes from the 1980s may have polybutylene pipe.
Hard water scales up water heaters and tankless units. Rare hard freezes, like February 2021, burst attic and exterior-wall pipes.
water: Round Rock draws from Lake Georgetown and Stillhouse Hollow Lake plus wells. The water is hard, so scale builds up in heaters and fixtures.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Look for gray pipe stamped PB2110.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Round Rock, Teravista, Forest Creek, Behrens Ranch, Brushy Creek, Paloma Lake and every other Round Rock neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Round Rock Building Inspection, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.a: Yes. Round Rock's lakes and wells sit in limestone country, so the water carries calcium and magnesium. A softener and yearly flushing protect water heaters.
